title: SCIM Setup surface — the last uncut leg of objectstack#11632, still measured at zero UI
body:
⛔ Read `objectstack-ai/objectstack#11632` before starting; this card is its scope item 5 and nothing more.

⚠️ **The `Blocked-by: objectstack#11632` line this card was filed with is WITHDRAWN — it was circular and it was my error.** This card is a **leg of** that epic, not a dependent of it; as written, neither could move until the other did. The epic is now owned by the PM session driving this card (takeover 2026-09-06 on the maintainer's instruction).

## Why this exists

The SCIM migration to stable `@better-auth/scim` **landed** — measured on objectstack `origin/main` 2026-09-06: the pin is `^1.7.2`, the seven stable models are present (`scimConnectionBinding` in 6 files), `storeSCIMToken` survives only as CHANGELOG entries and comments *recording its removal*, and the credential-at-rest posture keeps its own pin. Nine of the epic's ten sub-issues are closed.

**Scope item 5 — the net-new Setup surface — never was.** The epic charters it with the words *"objectui and cloud measured at zero SCIM UI today"*, and that measurement still holds: **0** files in this repository mention SCIM, and objectstack's `setup-nav.contributions.ts` names it **zero** times. It was never cut as a card, which is why nothing surfaced it in six days — an epic whose last leg was never cut is indistinguishable, from every queue view, from an epic that is finished.

## ⚠️ Before building: two things the epic leaves to be settled, ⛔ not to be decided by an implementer

1. **Is this still wanted as chartered?** The charter is from 2026-08-24 and the platform's SCIM story changed underneath it. ⛔ Do not build a surface nobody has re-confirmed; ask on the epic first.
2. **What does the surface administer, now that `sys_scim_provider` is retired** (#11757, closed)? Stable's own `scimConnectionBinding` is what remains, and the epic's *"Open before leg 2′"* section says which row the verifier reads was *"bounded design work inside scope item 1"*. If that landed, this surface administers the result of it; if it did not, ⛔ stop — a UI over an undecided storage shape is the wrong thing to build first.

## Scope, when the two above are settled

A Setup surface for SCIM provisioning: connection/binding administration, the operator-visible state of provisioned users and groups, and whatever the bearer-token lifecycle exposes **given that ObjectStack owns bearer storage outright** under an app-owned verifier (epic scope 8). ⛔ No credential is ever displayed after creation — the epic's scope 8 is explicit that credential-at-rest posture must be at parity or better, and a UI that renders a token would be a loosening.

⚠️ SCIM is default-off (`OS_SCIM_ENABLED`). The surface must be absent, not broken, on a deployment that has not enabled it — the `requiresService` / capability-gating pattern the Setup app already uses for organization-gated entries is the precedent.

## Acceptance

The surface is reachable only where SCIM is enabled; it administers real bindings against a running stack (⛔ not a mock); no credential is rendered after creation; and the framework-side declarations it needs (nav contribution, object/app metadata) land with it rather than as a follow-up — a nav entry pointing at a page that does not exist is worse than no entry.

Refs: objectstack#11632 (the epic, scope items 5 / 6 / 8) · objectstack#11757 (`sys_scim_provider` retired) · objectstack#11693 (the `managedConnections` refusal) · objectstack#11820 (blocked on the epic).



---

## ⭐ Precondition 2 is DISCHARGED — measured on objectstack `origin/main`, 2026-09-06

This card was filed saying *"⛔ stop — a UI over an undecided storage shape is the wrong thing to build first"*. The shape is decided, and here it is, so the implementer does not re-derive it:

`sys_scim_provider` is **retired** — not merely unused: it carries an ADR-0087 semantic migration entry, `packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/18.scim-provider-object-retired.ts`. Every remaining mention on the tree is a comment recording the retirement, that migration entry, or `cli/src/utils/unmanaged-tables.ts` noting that **cloud's control DB still carries the orphaned table** (that residue is `objectstack-ai/cloud#1739`, a separate card — ⛔ not this one's).

**What the surface administers**, bridged by `plugin-auth/src/objectql-adapter.ts` from stable's model names to platform objects:

| stable model | platform object |
|---|---|
| `scimConnectionBinding` | `sys_scim_connection_binding` |
| — (ObjectStack-owned) | `sys_scim_connection_credential` |
| `scimUser` / `scimGroup` / `scimGroupMember` | `sys_scim_user` / `sys_scim_group` / `sys_scim_group_member` |
| `scimSubject` | `sys_scim_subject` |
| `scimIdentityTombstone` | `sys_scim_identity_tombstone` |
| — | `sys_scim_projection_grant` |

⚠️ `sys_scim_connection_credential`'s own docblock says it is **deliberately not a resurrection of `sys_scim_provider`**, and that ordinary members are denied it entirely. ⇒ ⛔ The surface must not render or re-expose a credential after creation — epic scope 8 requires credential-at-rest posture at parity or better, and a UI that shows a token would be a loosening. That is a refusal, not a preference.

⇒ **Precondition 1 — is scope 5 still wanted as chartered — is the only one left**, and it is with the maintainer. This card is otherwise ready to dispatch.
